runtime_read.byte_for_byte: Identical to GAP9 GCC 7.1.1 (-march=rv32imcxgap9 -O2) in objdump, for no -mPE and for -mPE=0: CoreCount = 'lui a0,0x1a103; lw a0,18(a0)' (encodings 1a103537 01252503); CoreCount_m1 = the same load plus 'addi a0,a0,-1' (157d). With -mPE=8 both give li 8 / li 7. With -mPE=1 both give li 1 for CoreCount. For _m1, GCC emits the run-time read minus 1 and clang emits li 0 (the deliberate difference).
runtime_read.what_the_address_is: 0x1A103012 is NOT a core-count register on GAP9. In the public GAP9 SDK archi headers (rtos/pmsis/archi/chips/gap9/include/archi/properties.h:102-106, memory_map.h:182-186), 0x1A103000 is UDMA_CHAN_LIN_ADDR (SOC_PERIPHERALS 0x1A100000 + 0x3000), which holds the UDMA linear address-generator channel 0 registers (udma_core_lin_regs.h: SA_BUF0 0x0, SA_BUF1 0x4, SIZE 0x8, CURR_ADDR 0x14, BYTES_LEFT 0x18, CTRL 0x1c). Offset 0x12 is not a register, and a 32-bit read there is misaligned. In the GVSoC GAP9 model (gvsoc/gvsoc_gap/gap/gap9/soc.json), apb_ico maps 'udma' to 0x1A102000 with size 0x2000, so the read goes to the UDMA model. The GAP9 cluster core count is APB_SOC_CTRL INFO at 0x1A104000, field NB_CORES bits [31:16] (apb_soc_ctrl_regfields.h). GAP9 also exposes it as the compile-time constant ARCHI_CLUSTER_NB_PE=8 (properties.h:267).
runtime_read.why_gcc_uses_it: Public PULP GCC source (pulp-platform/pulp-riscv-gcc gcc/config/riscv/riscv-builtins.c:280-297) hard-codes it with the comment 'Gap8: (APB_SOC_CTRL_ADDR + 0x12) = SOC_PERIPHERALS_BASE_ADDR + 0x0300 + 0x12 / 0x1A100000 + 0x3000 + 0x12'. That is a stale, GAP8-era guess: even the public GAP8/PULP archi headers (pulp-platform/archi chips/gap and chips/pulp memory_map.h) have APB_SOC_CTRL at +0x4000 and UDMA at +0x2000. The run-time path is effectively dead code: the fold (riscv-builtins.c:779-788, 'if (_Pulp_PE>0) return build_int_cst(_Pulp_PE)') covers every SDK build, because the SDK always passes -mPE=8 -mFC=1 (for example examples/gap9/basic/gvsoc/user_launcher/Makefile:7, and every AutoTiler CMAKE_C_FLAGS dump). So the worker's GVSoC finding is right: GCC's own run-time read is wrong on GAP9 too. Matching GCC byte for byte (B107) is still the right fork policy: the old 'lw 0 & 0x12' was also wrong and matched nothing. The real fix for SDK apps is -mPE=8. A later, separate task could consider a GAP9-correct run-time read (lhu 0x1A104002). That would be a deliberate deviation from GCC and is not in scope here.

findings.mPE_semantics: Checked against GAP9 GCC myself. -mPE=8, -mPE=0x8 and -mPE=010 -mPE=8 (last one wins): 0 errors from either compiler across 8 contexts (static init, static init expression, file-scope array, _Static_assert, enum, bit-field, case label, static local) at -O0 and -O2. Without -mPE: the same 8 lines are errors in both. Bad values -1, abc, 8abc, +8, 0xg: both reject (clang with its standard 'unsupported argument', like -mrvv-vector-bits=). Empty value: GCC says 'missing argument', clang 'unsupported argument'. 2147483648 and 4294967297: GCC behaves erratically (run-time read, and 1), clang rejects them, which is acceptable. x86 target: error 'unsupported option'. cc1 -mPE=abc: 'invalid integral value'. GCC defines no macros for -mPE or -mFC (worker's -dM check; the GCC source only folds builtins). -mFC is not implemented, and nothing in this change interacts with it (the SDK wrapper must still drop -mFC=1, as recorded in other_errors_seen). The worker's contexts.txt (80 cases) matches my spot checks. The CoreCount_m1 -mPE=1 difference is confirmed as GCC's '_Pulp_PE>1' guard (riscv-builtins.c:785). Clang's fold to 0 only accepts programs GCC rejects and gives them the correct value: acceptable, and documented. C++ constexpr use works. Limitation (not blocking): with -fexperimental-new-constant-interpreter the fold does not happen, because clang/lib/AST/ByteCode/InterpBuiltin.cpp has no case. Upstream added bextr there separately in 851817885761. That interpreter is off by default in 20.
findings.upstream_edits: Three upstream files are edited, all minimal and justified. (a) ExprConstant.cpp: one 14-line case in IntExprEvaluator::VisitBuiltinCallExpr plus the Constexpr attribute, exactly upstream's pattern in 1c2ed36741c6 (verified: in llvmorg-20.1.8, not in llvmorg-19.1.7; adds a Constexpr attr and an ExprConstant case). No fork-owned alternative exists. A Sema-side AST rewrite of the call would need SemaExpr.cpp (also upstream) and is not upstream's pattern. A predefined function-like macro from the fork-owned Targets/RISCV.cpp would change -dM output, which GCC does not do, and is the same kind of hack as the survey's -D shim. (b) TargetOptions.h: one field, the same place as AMDGPU CodeObjectVersion; the AST evaluator can only see Target/LangOptions. (c) Clang.cpp: one self-contained block in AddRISCVTargetArgs, the only place RISC-V options are forwarded to cc1. The file is mapped to clang-driver. Rule 8/12: nothing upstream broke this. It is a pre-existing fork gap and defect, and the fork commits are cited. No oracle-cheating: no tests edited, no fork logic removed. The only removed line is the wrong ANDI pattern, and B107 plus the GCC comparison justify replacing it.
